title: Every core safety statement is in the label or justified
text: Each statement of the company core safety information (CCSI) should appear in the local label in substance. Where it does not, the difference is recorded in the deviation register with a justification. Non-CCSI parts of the CCDS (indications, dosing, pharmacology) may differ more freely, but the difference is still recorded.
simplified: The app suggests a match by key terms in the mapped sections and asks you to confirm it. Real alignment is a judgement about meaning, made by the labelling team.

title: A deviation needs a justification
text: A statement marked as deviating (or not applicable) needs a written reason, for example a local agency decision, an indication not approved in this market, or a local requirement.

title: The label is mapped to the current core data sheet
text: When a new CCDS version becomes effective, every local label is assessed against it. A label still mapped to an older version needs an impact assessment.
simplified: The app compares version numbers only.

title: Agency comments answered and labelling agreed
text: When the agency has commented on draft labelling, every comment needs a response (accept, partially accept, or decline with a reason), and the label is final only once the agency has agreed it.
simplified: The agency comments are scripted by the app; real review is a negotiation.

title: PMI headings in the proposed order
text: The proposed PMI has a fixed structure: the product name and use, then "Important Safety Information" with the subheadings Warnings, Do not take, Serious side effects and Tell your health care provider before taking, then "Common Side Effects", then "Directions for Use".
simplified: Proposed rule only (Watch). The app uses the headings described in public summaries of the proposal; check the final rule when it is published.

title: PMI fits on one page
text: The proposed PMI is a single page, with a 10-point minimum type size. FDA said it expects to grant waivers rarely.
simplified: The app estimates the page from a word count (about 520 words at 10 point on one page with headings). A real PMI is measured on the typeset page.

title: Directions for Use start with "Use exactly as prescribed"
text: The Directions for Use section starts with the statement "Use exactly as prescribed", followed by how to take the product, storage and disposal.

title: Boxed warning risks are in the PMI warnings
text: The PMI is based on the prescribing information. Each risk in the boxed warning should appear under Important Safety Information, Warnings.
simplified: The app looks for each boxed warning heading word (for example "infection") in the Warnings subsection.

title: No promotional wording
text: Patient labelling must not be promotional in tone, false or misleading. Words such as "best", "safest", "superior" or "breakthrough" do not belong in it.
simplified: The app looks for a short list of promotional words; a reviewer judges tone as a whole.

title: Plain language
text: Patient information should be written for patients. A reading level around grade 6 to 8 is a common target.
simplified: Reading grade is an estimate (Flesch-Kincaid style) and is shown as a hint only.
